Will Barcola hit the ground running at Anfield? The France winger registered 20 goal contributions in 49 games for Paris St-Germain last season.

A warm welcome from the skipper 😍 pic.twitter.com/95EAqUjYBn

The La Masia graduate secures a permanent move to Germany. Who knows how his career in England would have panned out had Chelsea not recalled him 25 days into his Sunderland loan at the beginning of last season...

Marc Guiu has completed a permanent transfer to Bundesliga side RB Leipzig. Everyone at Chelsea would like to thank Marc for his efforts during his time at the club and wish him every success as he begins the next chapter of his career with RB Leipzig.

What a couple of weeks it has been for Robert Sanchez. He came into this season as Chelsea’s No 1, but after a difficult start to the campaign and Emi Martinez’s arrival, reports suggest he could be moving away from Stamford Bridge on loan. Cesc Fabregas’s Como appears the probable destination.

Trevoh Chalobah, who left Chelsea for Como last month, has taken to his “secondary” Instagram account to post the following picture...

Meanwhile, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, striker flop Nick Woltemade is moving to Juventus on a season-long loan. The club’s record signing from as year ago at £64m is moving to Turin for a £3.5m loan fee with the Serie A squad covering the full cost of his wages.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

A post shared by Ligue 1 McDonald's (@ligue1mcdonalds)

The Leeds wide man has a medical booked with Fiorentina today. He made a handful of appearances for Daniel Farke’s side during pre-season but has not featured since the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

✈️ L'arrivo di Gnonto a Firenze ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/nEFngsyxQP

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Jayden Danns, who broke through three years ago and played in the 2024 League Cup final defeat of Chelsea, is attracting interest from clubs in Europe, who want to take him on loan. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1889. Thomas Tuchel reveals why Cole Palmer has been left out of England squad AGAIN

Thomas Tuchel has explained Cole Palmer is still paying the price for missing too many England camps after the Chelsea star was once again left out of his Three Lions squad.

Palmer was left out of the World Cup squad in the summer and withdrew from the group for the extended international break in September and October due to injury.

Tuchel warned it was a ‘missed opportunity’ for Palmer at the time, insisting he ‘misses way too many camps’ with other players moving ahead of him in the pecking order as a result.

Palmer has played almost every minute of Chelsea’s Premier League campaign this term with his injury problems from last season seemingly behind him.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

But Tuchel made the decision on Friday to leave him out of the squad for upcoming Nations League games against Croatia and Spain with Jobe Bellingham and Fulham’s Josh King named ahead of him.

Speaking on Friday, Tuchel explained King’s versatility was a key reason for his inclusion ahead of Palmer. Morgan Rogers and Morgan Gibbs-White also also vying for the no10 spot with Tuchel explaining the group that impressed him training last month keep their places on merit.

‘It is enough no10s [in the squad] and we stick with guys who were in camp because camp was excellent for the two-and-a-half weeks we had together,’ Tuchel said.

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), James Trafford (Leeds United), Jason Steele (Brighton)

Defenders: Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Marc Guehi (Man City), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Jarrell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Ben White (Arsenal)

Midfielders: Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), Josh King (Fulham), James Garner (Everton), Elliot Anderson (Man City), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal)

Forwards: Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea)

‘The impact of other players was immense and that’s why we stick with the group and all the offensive players. We have Josh King in there but I also want to see him on both wings, he can play all four positions, that is basically the reason.’

Tuchel added: ‘Everyone is desperate to play for England and Cole is no exception.

‘But we are speaking about a player who is not in camp and on the other hand it counts when you are in camp and I said it last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress.

‘It was a long camp, two-and-a-half weeks and the boys who were in the camp built something extraordinary. That’s why the credit and trust goes to them.

‘It’s not personal and we will never assume Cole is not in the mindset to play for his country but the competition is on and the players from that camp keep their place.’

#1888. Pitcher perfect: Charlie’s strike hands Steyning Town victory over Horley

Town were without several key men so made a few adjustments to the team – but still lined up looking strong, showing the increasing competition for places.

The first half was one that certainly saw Steyning in the ascendancy; however they were unable to turn possession to decent opportunities as both keepers remained largely untested.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The game sprang into life minutes before half-time as the busy Leo Ginger cut in from the left and let rip a stunning dipping strike from 25 yards that flew into the top right hand corner off the post.

What a great way to go into half-time… or so we thought. The visitors had other ideas as they hit back almost immediately breaking well at the other end of the pitch culminating in a fine finish into the top of the net by Abdulahi Abdulazeez.

The second period followed much of the pattern of the first, with the Barrowmen having the bulk of possession and playing some good football but lacking a bit of cutting edge.

The defining moment of the match came with 18 minutes to go as Charlie Pitcher broke down the right, taking a floating through ball superbly in his stride with a couple of great touches before sweeping home the winner in style. A great goal to win a less-than-great game.

Town saw out the remainder of the game with minimal fuss as they added three vital points to their league tally. The day was pretty much about grinding at a result when not at your best and overall it was really positive to do that when other games have got away from the team late on this season.

Steyning are 15th and next up – on Saturday – is a big test away to high-flying Hastings United.

#1887. Hearts unbeaten home record obliterated as swashbuckling Falkirk earn 31-year first

Rampant Falkirk obliterated Hearts’ 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership with a stunning 5-2 win at Tynecastle as they leapfrogged the Jambos into third place.

Wouter Vrancken’s beleaguered side, missing 11 players through injury amid a gruelling fixture list, were in disarray as the swashbuckling Bairns romped into a five-goal lead early in the second half through Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hearts hit back through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty, but Falkirk were well worthy of making it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time since 1995.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle for Hearts since April 2025. To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos, who have won just two of their last 11 matches, lost yet another senior player as Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

There were two changes to the Hearts side that started Thursday’s Conference League defeat to Thun as Stephen Kingsley and Guendouz were replaced by Yan Dhanda and Landry Kabore.

Falkirk boss John McGlynn, named manager of the month for October, made one enforced change from the side that defeated Celtic last Sunday as Jack McMillan took over from injured right-back Ryan Strain.

The Bairns seized the lead in the fourth minute. After Murrell’s close-range effort from Scott Tanser’s cross was brilliantly saved by Beau Reus, Barbrook reacted quickest to drill home a low, angled finish from eight yards out.

Hearts threatened an equaliser in the 10th minute, but Kabore’s effort on the turn from the edge of the six-yard box was superbly blocked by Scott Bain.

Falkirk doubled their lead in the 17th minute after the hosts were caught wide open on the counter-attack. Dhanda’s shot from distance was charged down, allowing the Bairns to break swiftly, with Brad Spencer weighting his pass perfectly for Eames, who fired past the exposed Reus.

Braga thought he had pulled one back for Hearts in the 20th minute, but it was ruled out for handball.

Falkirk took full advantage of this reprieve by adding a third in the 33rd minute as Murrell peeled off Fagan-Walcott at the back post to nod home Deniss Melniks’ cross from the right.

The visitors struck again in first-half stoppage-time as Henderson curled high past Reus after Tanser’s corner broke to him just inside the box.

As jeers rained down from an irate home support, Vrancken replaced midfielders Laurent Mendy and Dhanda with Guendouz and Matthew Gillies for the start of the second half.

But within two minutes of the restart Falkirk notched again as Murrell fired home after being set up by Ethan Ross.

Hearts got off the mark when Guendouz drilled in his first goal for the club from just inside the box in the 50th minute.

Braga then tucked away a penalty in the 74th minute after Guendouz was tripped by Lewis Neilson, but it was not enough to prevent a third straight defeat for the Jambos.

#1886. Why Jobe Bellingham received England call-up instead of Kobbie Mainoo

Jobe Bellingham has been given his first England call-up with Thomas Tuchel claiming Kobbie Mainoo’s recent injury problems cost him a place in the latest squad.

The Borussia Dortmund midfielder will join his brother Jude for Nations League games against Croatia and Spain having impressed Tuchel and his staff this season.

He joins James Garner, Elliot Anderson, Declan Rice and Myles Lewis-Skelly as Tuchel’s central midfield options with Manchester United star Mainoo among the list of high profile absentees which once again includes Cole Palmer and Phil Foden.

Mainoo was part of England’s World Cup squad but did not play a single minute. He was included in the group for the extended international break in September and October but was among a spate of injury withdrawals.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

Mainoo has been first choice in midfield under Michael Carrick when available, missing four of his side’s 14 games through injury. He returned to the team against Chelsea last weekend before playing a key role in the midweek victory over Roma.

Speaking on Friday, Tuchel said Mainoo’s injury last month was a key reason behind the decision not to select him with Jobe getting the nod instead.

‘I think Kobbie has had a difficult spell and missed a lot of matches,’ Tuchel said. ‘In the meantime it was Jobe who impressed in the same level of time and that is what we want.

‘The door is always open for younger ones to overtake and make their mark but that is just a sign of the level of competition in central midfield.’

Jobe meanwhile will have the chance to play alongside his brother in games against Croatia and Spain with Tuchel envisaging a more defensive role for the younger sibling.

Goalkeepers: Jordan Pickford (Everton), James Trafford (Leeds United), Jason Steele (Brighton)

Defenders: Ezri Konsa (Arsenal), Marc Guehi (Man City), Jarrad Branthwaite (Everton), Trent Alexander-Arnold (Real Madrid), Lewis Hall (Newcastle United), Jarrell Quansah (Bayer Leverkusen), Djed Spence (Inter Milan), Ben White (Arsenal)

Midfielders: Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid), Jobe Bellingham (Borussia Dortmund), Josh King (Fulham), James Garner (Everton), Elliot Anderson (Man City), Eberechi Eze (Arsenal), Myles Lewis-Skelly (Arsenal), Declan Rice (Arsenal)

Forwards: Harry Kane (Bayern Munich), Morgan Gibbs-White (Nottingham Forest), Dominic Calvert-Lewin (Leeds United), Anthony Gordon (Barcelona), Rio Ngumoha (Liverpool), Morgan Rogers (Chelsea)

‘We see him in central midfield, not as offensive as Jude,’ Tuchel said.

‘It’s an incredible achievement for the family and the brothers. I was very happy to give him the call and I saw his excitement straight away in his smile. It was a very nice phone call.

‘We see him in central midfield so he is one of five players who have for central midfield. He is a more defensive player than his brother, good physique good on the ball, very physical player and can keep possession.

‘Now it is on him because we only have Tuesday and Wednesday to prepare for the Thursday match.’

#1885. Moretto: Krösche ‘continues to push’ to bring Hardung with him to Milan – the situation

Matteo Moretto has confirmed that Markus Krösche will look to try and bring Timmo Hardung with him to AC Milan.

In the past few days, there have been reports from a number of sources claiming that Gerry Cardinale is finally going to get the man that he has wanted for a few months. Krösche – who left Eintracht Frankfurt last month – has an agreement in place to come in and lead the management.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

The issue of the compensation to be paid to Eintracht seems to have been resolved, so now the main question concerns whether someone will come in to help him as a sporting director, another position vacant in the current set-up.

In a video on their YouTube channel, Fabrizio Romano and Matteo Moretto gave some updates on the plans for Milan moving forward, including the restructuring of the management. MilanNews relayed the words of the latter.

“The Krosche deal has been a rollercoaster ride. AC Milan had practically already finalised the deal before the summer window. It was also a question of timing and also of finances, as Eintracht Frankfurt were asking for much higher compensation than what Milan has paid so far, or will soon pay,” he said.

“Anyway, here we go: Marcus Krösche will be ​​Milan’s new Head of Football. Milan will pay compensation of between €3-4m. Official confirmation, as far as I know, will arrive in early January. However, it’s clear that Krosche will already begin working behind the scenes for AC Milan in the coming months, and then he will officially be the new Rossoneri director from January.

“Krösche fits into an organisational and sporting structure that Cardinale had already thought of once he had restructured Milan from scratch. There are other figures within the Milan structure, such as Bobby Gardiner, Almstadt, who from what I understand will remain, but it is clear that Krosche’s figure will be predominant and on a sporting level he will be the one with the most power.

“From what I understand, Krösche continues to push to try to bring in a sporting director who can add to the organisational chart and the name that continues to buzz in Krösche’s head is certainly that of his right-hand man Timmo Hardung, who is the current sporting director of Eintracht. However, it is still to be seen whether Timo Hardung will remain at Eintracht 100%.

“It is true that Eintracht are trying to give him as much power as possible, but I do not rule out Hardung’s exit starting from January or February. Milan remain on the lookout, other German clubs such as Nürnberg, Hannover or Hamburg are also interested in Hardung. Milan wants try inserting another figure, maybe a little further forward.”

#1881. This is an embarrassment – Wouter Vrancken rages after Hearts humiliation

Wouter Vrancken condemned a “ridiculous” first-half display from his sorry Hearts side as their 18-month unbeaten home record in the Scottish Premiership was ripped apart by ruthless Falkirk.

The beleaguered Jambos, who went into the game without 11 players through injury following a gruelling run of fixtures, endured a dismal afternoon as the Bairns raced into a 4-0 half-time lead on their way to a 5-2 victory at Tynecastle.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Finley Barbrook, Owen Eames, Liam Henderson and Jacob Murrell’s double had the visitors 5-0 up within 47 minutes before Hearts reduced the deficit through substitute Sabri Guendouz and a Claudio Braga penalty.

It was a first league defeat at Tynecastle since April 2025 for the Jambos, who have now won just two of their last 11 matches in all competitions.

“This is an embarrassment, the first half for sure,” said Vrancken. “Always doubting, always doing things half-half, in possession, out of possession, everything, and such easy goals again.

“When you give those easy goals, then you cannot win a game. It’s childish goals and cannot happen on this level. Those simple things, they are the basics actually in these situations.

“It’s crazy, crazy, and everybody – me, staff, players – have to take responsibility in those things. This is ridiculous.”

To exacerbate their grim predicament, the Jambos lost yet another senior player as defender Malachi Fagan-Walcott limped off in the second half.

“This also makes me a bit angry, because now we lose Mal again,” said Vrancken.

“Hopefully it’s not too bad, but still we had to replace him there, because he was one of the guys who were good in the game and in the last games actually he had a really consistent, good level.”

Hearts were leapfrogged into third place by Falkirk, who made it five top-flight wins in a row for the first time in 31 years.

“I’ve never been 5-0 up here before,” said Bairns manager John McGlynn. “First half we were outstanding. A great start to the game for us to get the goal so early.

“It was well documented about the Hearts injuries and, coming off the back of the game on Thursday night (in Thun), it was always going to be difficult for them.

“We had to smell blood and we had to go for it and that’s exactly what happened. The goals and our play were outstanding in the first half. We won every duel, we won everything all over the park.

“We got ourselves 4-0 up at half-time, which is dreamland. At 3pm, we never expected to be 4-0 up at half-time and certainly not 5-0 up a few minutes into the second half, which was another really good goal in transition.

“Hearts had a lot at the ball and dominated the second period, but we’re taking 5-2 every day of the week, make no mistake about it. It jumps us up into third place.

“Winning five on the trot has not been done since 1995, Jim Jefferies’ team, so I’m delighted for everyone at the football club that we’ve managed to equal that record.”

#1876. Why Kasper Hogh would not have taken Celtic penalty as Mika Baur injury addressed

Martin O’Neill admitted he would not have let Kasper Hogh take a second half penalty that Benjamin Nygren ended up failing to score in any case as Celtic squeezed past Kilmarnock at Parkhead.

The striker’s goal drought was extended to 16 games and he’s still to open his account at home for his new club. Defender Liam Scales was the match winner after converting a cross from Camilo Dusan in the 25th minute.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Hogh had earlier endured the heartbreak of seeing a goal chalked off for a foul committed earlier in the move by Mika Baur and he snatched at a chance shortly afterwards when one-on-one with Kilmarnock ‘keeper Nico Mantl.

Hogh worked hard and was named man-of-the-match but was replaced after 70 minutes. Celtic were awarded a penalty shortly afterwards and many Celtic fans lamented Hogh not still being on the pitch to take it. However, O’Neill confirmed this wouldn’t have happened even if he had been available.

Nygren duly saw Mantl make an excellent save from his effort from 12 yards to keep Kilmarnock in the game. The visitors came close to equalising right at the death when Ieuan Owen failed to connect with a cross right in front of goal.

“We all thought Kasper had got off the mark,” said O’Neill, with reference to the goal that wasn’t. “We all thought that for about 35 seconds. I think myself that maybe he would have scored the next one had the first one counted but he worked exceptionally hard for us. I was pleased the team dug it out.

“We got the penalty but had he still been on the pitch I would not have asked him to take it. He might have missed. As it turned out, we did miss.

“In front of goal, it is proving a difficult one for him,” O'Neill added. “But he has worked exceptionally hard in the game, as he did on Thursday night (v Besiktas). I think things will come, honestly. He thought he had broken the spell but his hold up play was much, much better.”

Hogh received a warm ovation when he was replaced after 70 minutes by James Forrest. “I think that’s encouraging,” said O’Neill. “If you have the crowd behind you, if you’re working hard, they will forgive some other things. Now I am not saying that will last forever….Of course strikers live and die by their goals. But he feels we all believe in him in the dressing room, that’s encouraging for him.”

O’Neill stressed he had not seen a replay of the incident involving Baur that meant Hogh’s goal after 13 minutes was ruled off after a VAR check. Referee John Beaton was called to the monitor and he very abruptly signalled he was disallowing the strike.

“I have genuinely not seen it back because the little screen we have on the touchline is too small for me,” he said. “I can only go with what the lads were saying, they thought it was touch and go.”

O’Neill also revealed that Baur, who limped off near the end, had suffered ankle damage and has been booked in for a scan. The midfielder is due to join up with the Germany Under-21s in the international break.

“He’s in the treatment room,” he said. “His ankle is really sore and we don’t know the damage. We’ll wait until tomorrow to get a scan. Gosh, I’d hope he won’t be out terribly long but I don't know at the moment. He’s been great for us considering he’s not the tallest. He’d be about ten stone maybe not even that but his work rate is incredible. His overall reading of the game is really good and he’s not frightened.”

#1875. Rockettes put 10 past Portchester – the match in pictures

The result leaves them second in the table with four wins and a draw from their opening five matches.

Bec Bell-Thorns set up two attacks early on with her runs and crosses from the right. First Kate Delilis diverted a chance over the bar and then a similar move soon after saw Millie Carter shoot high and wide just 3 minutes in. Aimee Hall-Guy did well in the Bognor area following a cross from the right but diverted wide from close range.

Bognor took the lead on 12 minutes when a corner fell to Sophia Poling who nodded it in despite a defender's efforts on the line. The Rockettes extended their lead on 15 minutes as Kate Delillis fired it in off a defender following Lucie Wright's freekick cross. Sophie Humphrey also hit the left post after a short run as Bognor dominated the opening 20 minutes.

Nicole Robinson saved comfortably from Hall-Guy's strike from outside the area. Lily West put a neat through ball to Char Heanen but her powerful strike was pushed over confidently by Robinson on 26 minutes. Lucie Selvester did well to cross the ball into the area to find Sophie Humphrey but after twisting and turning she brought out a good save by Sofie Harris.

Elena Butcher clipped the crossbar with her cross moments later for the visitors. On 33 minutes Poling hit a long range freekick directly high and wide as Bognor maintained their lead. Bognor went three goals up in the 35th minute. The visitors failed to clear their lines from Wright's corner before the ball fell to Humphrey who blasted it high into the roof of the net.

Bognor got their fourth goal on 40 minutes. A fine pass out wide onto the left found Lucie Wright in space and shen ran onto it before firing it over the goalkeeper and into the net. It got better for the hosts as Humphrey netted her second of the afternoon, following up the rebound from a previous strike on 44 minutes. HT 5-0.

After half time Niamh Andersson replaced Bell-Thorns.

Humphrey turned in the area quickly and forced a save over the bar from Harris. Humphrey studded in from close range for Bognor's 6th goal of the afternoon. It was scrappy in defence for the visitors who failed to clear the danger on 48 minutes. On 56 minutes Alice Gue was replaced by Ellie Jefkins.

Bognor made it seven on 58 minutes when Humphrey netted her fourth of the day following a low cross. Delillis set up Freya Boxer but after a nice run she hit the side netting with her strike. Bognor made another change on 62 minutes as Wright came off for Clara Castanheira.

Elena Williams hit a free-kick directly into Robinson's arms in a rare chance for the visitors. Carter's corner kick on the right bounced back out for a goal kick off the frame of goal moments later. Bognor got their 8th in the 66th minute as Humphrey closed down the ball before passing it square to Boxer in the box and she made no mistake, netting it along the deck and in.

Bognor got their ninth on 69 minutes. Andersson placed it nicely beyond defence for Delillis who fired it past the goalkeeper. On 70 minutes Talliah Anderson replaced Sophie Humphrey. Good work from Carter saw her pass back to Castanheira who curled it into the middle where Andersson was waiting but she diverted it wide of goal.

A cross from the left by Castanheira found Boxer in the box and she fired it high and in for Bognor's tenth goal on 76 minutes. A high corner bounced off Elena Williams and into the net for the visitors first goal of the afternoon as a consolation. The visitors also hit the post moments later as the goal perked up the opposition in for the first time in the second half.

Gue came back on for Macie Downs on 86 minutes in a rolling substitution. But despite more chances for Boxer for the Rockettes towards the end it was a comprehensive victory for the Bognor women's side.

They travel to Andover New Street on Sunday, November 15, at 2pm before playing at home on Sunday 22 against AFC Varsity with kick off at 2pm.

According to Spanish outlet Sport, Balde’s agent, Jorge Mendes, is already sounding out interest from clubs around Europe ahead of the January window.

And it is said that Balde’s preference is a move to the Premier League, with Liverpool, Aston Villa and United among the clubs interested.

Italian clubs Roma and Juventus have reportedly met with Mendes to enquire about a move for Balde, but the player’s salary demands could prove an obstacle.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

United had been actively looking to strengthen at left-back in the summer to provide support and competition for Luke Shaw, and were linked with a move to Balde in the closing weeks of the summer window.

Michael Carrick’s side are expected to resume that search in the New Year, particularly given Luke Shaw’s injury, which has seen Diogo Dalot forced to play at left-back.

Last month, Carrick said the club would look to strengthen in the January transfer window, telling Sky Sports: When the next transfer window comes, you want to plan and you want to make the best of it.

‘Whatever that looks like at this stage, we don’t quite know. But without doubt, there’s opportunity because the transfer window is open.

‘So we’ll definitely be looking at that and trying to come out stronger in whatever way that looks like.’

#1872. Celtic pyschodrama engulfing team as VAR delivers mother of all smackdowns

Celtic built on their uplifting midweek victory over Besiktas but found the going hard against Neil McCann’s well-drilled team.

The champions possibly should have won by more than just Liam Scales’ 25th minute goal. However, Kasper Hogh’s woes are threatening to become a psychodrama afflicting the entire team.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

The Dane isn’t playing badly. Never mind the goal he scored after 13 minutes that was then very harshly chopped off for a foul in the build-up. Another shot midway through the second half appeared goal-bound until a heroic block from substitute MJ Kamson-Kamara deflected the ball over the bar. Events seem to be conspiring against him.

Hogh was subbed off with 20 minutes left to very warm applause. He was sitting on the bench when he heard his name surprisingly announced as the man of the match. If this was an attempt to encourage the striker, it seemed a bit cringingly overboard.

Hogh was also on the bench when Celtic were awarded a penalty after 75 minutes so couldn’t grab the ball in an effort to put everything to bed. Nygren accepted the responsibility instead and saw Nico Mantl make a brilliant diving block to keep Kilmarnock in the game.

The fans certainly appreciated Hogh’s endeavours and clearly believe that while the statistics books might state otherwise, he has already morally broken his Parkhead duck.

His neat finish was cruelly chalked off - after the Dane had completed the understandably comprehensive celebration routine - for a foul by Mika Baur in the build-up that very few saw. Referee John Beaton nevertheless seemed very sure having been called to his monitor and spent little time deliberating.

A clearly agitated Hogh then wasted a good chance to score shortly afterwards although credit should go to Mantl, the true man of the match, for blocking with his foot when the striker had just the keeper to beat. Mantl's later penalty stop - after a VAR check confirmed a handball by Aaron Tshibola had taken place inside the box – meant bottom-of-the-table Kilmarnock were still fighting until the end.

They came so close to taking the point their efforts certainly deserved. With the clock having ticked into the four minutes of additional time, substitute Eric Ring reached the byline and swung in a cross that Ieuan Owen somehow failed to connect with in the middle.

As for Celtic, with their No. 9 seemingly so out of touch and luck, their No. 5 stepped in. Scales scored the kind of goal that is eluding Hogh at present after he got on the end of Duran’s floated cross. The ball kissed the crossbar before landing in the net. That’s three goals for the defender this season – equal with Hogh.

A planned period of silence to commemorate the war dead was cut short before kick-off due to the volume of booing in the stadium. Beaton barely gave it ten seconds before blowing his whistle. It all felt a little unsettling with Celtic taking longest to get themselves focused, at the risk of very nearly conceding the first goal. As was the case at the death, the visitors came close to scoring right at the start. Tom Lowery even had two bites at the cherry, with Celtic goalkeeper Sam Johnstone the equal to his efforts both times.

Celtic sought to take advantage of the let-off and immediately got on with the seeming job in hand: helping Hogh get off the mark at Parkhead. Nygren tried to place a cross on his head after eight minutes but the striker was crowded out. It was almost as if the team had been specifically set up to let Hogh score. And he did. 4.13pm, the moment Celtic Park had been waiting for – or so it seemed.

With Jota, making his first start since April 2025, and Camilo Duran either side of Hogh and Nygren in the space behind, it ought to have been a centre-forward’s dream. Especially given all these players seemingly had one aim in mind: feed the Hogh.

Parkhead exploded with joy unconfined. Duran slipped the ball through to Nygren, who swivelled and played in Hogh. The Dane could not miss and to be fair, he didn’t. A very composed finish into the corner had him pointing to the heavens and crossing himself and making all manner of gestures of gratitude before VAR delivered the mother of all smackdowns: Goal disallowed.

Celtic secured the three points in the end, albeit with one or two scares. They have reached the latest international break in marginally better shape than last time, when successive Rangers defeats meant Martin O’Neill’s job seemed in very real jeopardy.

#1871. 'Provoked' - Brentford's Keith Andrews makes Chema Andres claim after Igor Thiago red card at Brighton

Brentford boss Keith Andrews questioned the use of VAR in the Premier League after Igor Thiago’s first-half dismissal proved costly in a 2-0 defeat at high-flying Brighton.

Bees striker Thiago was initially shown a yellow card by referee Michael Oliver after reacting to a shirt pull and subsequent push from Albion midfielder Chema Andres, who was also booked.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

But the punishment was upgraded to red on review as match official Oliver deemed the Brazil international used “force” to push his opponent in the face with a raised arm.

Brentford’s only other league defeat this term came after Yehor Yarmoliuk was shown a first-half red card in last month’s 2-1 home loss to Liverpool.

Andrews accepted his players must take responsibility for their conduct but questioned the circumstances surrounding both incidents.

“We’ve lost two games in the league this season and both have been when we’ve gone down to 10 men, so you need to analyse yourself first clearly,” he said.

“On both scenarios, we can do better. On both scenarios, the opposition player has been the one to provoke the situation and antagonise our player and react towards our player in an aggressive way.

“Players’ reactions now mean everything. I’m going to reiterate it: we should do better. But the game is in a state now of a place I don’t particularly like. We’ll have to have a look at that because it’s costing us.”

Brentford were already trailing at the time of Thiago’s sending-off following a stunning long-range opener from Brighton midfielder Diego Gomez.

Disgruntled away fans chanted “2-0 to the referee” and “Michael Oliver, it’s all about you” after Pascal Gross doubled Albion’s lead with a 42nd-minute penalty awarded for Keane Lewis-Potter’s shirt pull on Luka Vuskovic.

Andrews, who felt his side should have been “cuter” in the penalty incident, was frustrated Oliver was sent to the pitch-side monitor before changing his initial decision on Thiago.

“I’m struggling to believe in this day and age where we see the referee’s call on pitch and the bar of where they’re given the licence to referee in-game, which is what I should think it should be, but he’s been sent to the screen,” he said.

“We play on the edge, we’re a team that likes to play on the edge, I want us to be on the edge. But it clearly cost us.”

Brighton climbed to second after marking their return to the Amex Stadium following five successive away matches with a comfortable victory.

Gomez lashed into the top-left corner with his left foot to follow up his goal from the halfway line in last month’s 5-0 thrashing of rivals Crystal Palace.

Seagulls head coach Fabian Hurzeler said: “It’s a funny story because yesterday he trained shooting with the left foot and I couldn’t see him scoring today with this left foot – the shots weren’t great.

“I asked him after the game where he got this quality from overnight. It’s a huge improvement in a very short period.”

Albion’s win was a seventh from 10 top-flight games and lifted them above Manchester City and back to within five points of leaders Arsenal.

Asked when Seagulls supporters can start getting really excited, Hurzeler said: “They should be always excited if they watch our game, and that’s our job to make them excited.

“I always say they can dream, they can have high expectations on us, but these are things we can’t control.”

#1870. Amorim offers honest Milan reflection: “We’re not ready, we’re far from being a really strong team”

Ruben Amorim continued the criticism of his AC Milan side after their dismal defeat to Ferencvaros, branding them ‘not ready’ to compete on multiple fronts.

Amorim made the decision to enact six changes to the starting line-up from the team that beat Inter convincingly in the derby at the weekend, but it backfired as his team never got going last night and were well-beaten by the Hungarians.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

It is reported that after the game the Portuguese coach gave a long speech to his players about their attitude and effort levels. Milan remain incredibly inconsistent on this front, as they continue to alternate very encouraging performances with disastrous and listless ones.

Amorim laid into his team during an interview with Sky after the final whistle, and then he spoke to the CBS Sports Golazo studio shortly afterwards. The exchange was transcribed by MilanNews.

Yesterday you were talking about identity, about character. Was this the difference?

“Yes, technically, tactically, and above all mentally, they were superior and deserved to win. Today we weren’t ready to play professional football, and I felt it. We need to look within ourselves and do better.”

And in the Champions League the level would be even higher…

“We have to focus on the small details, without thinking about the Champions League or anything like that. We just have to focus on improving the more specific aspects of football: the mentality, the heart, the passion. We have to improve on that.”

What is Ferencvaros’ level in European football, how do you rate them?

“I don’t know, it depends on the opponent, but they’re doing very well. They have four wins in four games, a clear identity, and today they were superior to us.”

What did this match tell you about Milan?

“That we’re not ready. We’re not ready, we’re far from being a really strong team. We have moments, in some games, where we’re really strong, but then we can’t maintain our level, especially mentally. So this game told me and all of us that we’re not ready to be a very strong team.”

During the first half, I noticed you were very energetic on the sidelines, and then it almost seemed like you stopped giving directions. Can you tell there’s a certain lack of understanding within the team and that they’re not playing the way you’d like?

“No, I just do what I feel at the time, and sometimes I don’t do certain things just for show. We didn’t play well, that’s for sure; we had a completely different attitude in the last league game, while today we weren’t mentally prepared to fight for the win, and that’s what we need to work on.”

If there hadn’t been the derby at the weekend, do you think this match would have gone better?

“I have no idea, it doesn’t matter. It doesn’t matter, we have to be ready to play every three days in different competitions. So it doesn’t matter if we had a match before or not. I think we have to improve a lot in all aspects of the game.”

Torriani played his first match as a starter. How do you rate his performance today?

“I think he did well in the first half. He had a difficult time with a pass, but Lorenzo doesn’t bear any responsibility for the team’s performance. In fact, in the first half he gave us time to try to make some changes in the second half. So Lorenzo just has to keep working. We have to improve as a team to be stronger.”

#1865. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

The Swede’s two early goals have earned Liverpool all three points at Portman Road and the travelling Liverpool fans are singing his name. Isak’s fellow teammates are pushing him towards the travelling fans to take their adulation as they belt out his name.

The final whistle goes at Portman Road and Andoni Iraola picks up his first win as Liverpool boss with a 2-0 victory thanks to Isak’s quickfire double inside the opening 10 minutes. Like they did two seasons ago, Liverpool win 2-0 at Portman Road.

Enciso has a late shot from the edge of the box but it goes wide of the far post.

McAteer shoots from range but there is not enough power to trouble Alisson, who makes the save down to his right.

A late change from Liverpool as Koumas replaces Wirtz.

Due to that VAR review for the Liverpool penalty that was not, there will probably be five or six added minutes.

Clarke’s shot from just outside the Liverpool penalty area takes a deflection off his teammate Diop and goes wide.

Davis is getting a fair bit of joy down Ipswich’s left and the ball has been on to him quite a few times. He is being afforded too much space by Liverpool to get crosses in.

Davis and Ipswich can count themselves very, very lucky. It would have been a penalty but Szoboszlai was offside when the original ball was played. For the second time tonight, an offside call massively goes in Ipswich’s favour; one to deny Isak a hat-trick and now to deny Liverpool a penalty. A massive let-off for Ipswich.

Barcola’s first few touches in a Liverpool shirt are pretty good down the left. He is playing in his most natural position of wide left, with Gakpo now down the middle and Szoboszlai on the right.

Gary O’Neil is going to make a double change as Clarke and Flemming come on, with the latter making his debut. Maeda and Emersonn come off.

So, here comes from the £123m Frenchman as Barcola enters the fray for his Liverpool debut. Gravenberch also comes on. There will be no first Liverpool hat-trick for Isak as he heads off, as does Munoz.

Bradley Barcola comes on to make his Liverpool debut! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/PjO78nlcqj

Andoni Iraola must be ripping his air out with the lack of composure and control from his side since half-time. It is no wonder he is about to turn to his bench and a certain Frenchman.

Enciso is given far too much space to drive towards the Liverpool box before shooting but Alisson makes the save. Liverpool, despite being 2-0 up, have showed a real lack of composure since the break.

If trends are anything to go by, Bradley Barcola will be introduced in the next three or four minutes. Andoni Iraola likes to change things around the hour mark and if the Frenchman warms up anymore, he will nearly overheat.

Kerkez is the latest player into the book for a foul on Fatawu.

Fatawu receives it out on the right for Ipswich and cuts inside onto his preferred left foot before curling an effort towards the far post but it goes wide.

Jacquet takes a heavy touch from a high ball and ends up taking out Emersonn, which earns the Frenchman a booking.

Liverpool work it well down their left as Isak plays it into Gakpo, who drives towards the Ipswich box. He plays it across the face of the penalty area to Szboszblai, who flicks it first time into the path of Wirtz. The German’s effort takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger finds a free Mac Allister at the front post but the Argentine’s header is straight at Scherpen. That was a good chance for Mac Allister.

We are back under way at Portman Road. No changes for either side at the break.

We have just seen replays of a possible penalty shout for Liverpool right at the end of the first half for a foul on Gakpo by Fatawu and it looked a decent shout.

Perhaps if Liverpool were playing a team with a bit more savvy, the 2-0 scoreline they currently protect would have been in jeopardy. Ipswich have put some nice moves together and had half chances but not enough to really turn the screw. Andoni Iraola, certainly, has been unhappy at times and it is becoming a trademark to see him spin around from the technical area in disgust when a ball has been squandered. In the main, though, he can be satisfied with this opening 45 minutes. Liverpool should be winning from here.

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Wirtz feeds a lovely pass into the left channel to pick out the run of Isak into the Ipswich box but Diop comes in with a crucial challenge.

Two added minutes at the end of this first half.

Araujo slices a clearance out of play for an Ipswich corner. A real gift for the home side as Araujo was not under any real pressure.

Isak should head away at the near post but it comes to Mac Allister to clear away.

A chance for Wirtz as the ball falls to the German on the edge of the Ipswich box but his shot is saved by Scherpen down to his left.

Enciso is the first Ipswich player into the book tonight for delaying a restart.

Szoboszlai, for the third time in the half, shoots from range. Again, the Hungarian gets plenty of power on it but fortunately for Scherpen it is straight at him.

Enciso turns neatly not far outside the Liverpool box and then shoots but slices the shot a fair way wide.

Tommy Elphick, a member of Andoni Iraola’s coaching staff, is booked for his protestations. Liverpool are not happy with some of the fouls being given against them and then some that are not given for them, including a clear foul from Emersonn on Van Dijk that was not penalised.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

Mac Allister receives a pass from Wirtz and, from just outside the box, decides to shoot but his effort goes just over. Scherpen did appear to have it covered anyway.

A crucial intervention from Araujo. Enciso drives down Ipswich’s right after Fatawu’s header, with Mac Allister tracking back. From the right side of the Liverpool box, Enciso’s deflected cross comes towards Maeda at the far post but Araujo makes an important clearance.

Moments later, Davis again meets a Fatawu cross at the far post but his header is off target.

Fatawu’s dangerous cross from the right all the way to the back post finds Davis, who heads back across goal. Emersonn takes a touch with his chest on the edge of the six-yard box before shooting but Jacquet is on hand to make a crucial block. Ipswich though do have their first corner of the game.

Lukic clips it in and Alisson should punch away with ease. However, the ball comes off Gakpo and, very fortunately for Alisson, the ball gets trapped between his own legs and he can gather. Alisson will be a relieved man.

Szoboszlai sends another powerful shot from range towards the goal and forces Scherpen into another decent save. Ipswich are not helping themselves at times by just giving the ball away inside their own half.

Szoboszlai comes close to adding a third for Liverpool. Fatawu inexplicably gives the ball away inside his own half before Mac Allister plays it forward to Szoboszlai, who takes just one touch before firing towards goal. Scherpen gets down well to his right to make the save.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

The first booking of the game goes the way of Mac Allister, who is booked slightly harshly for a foul on Enciso.

Moments later, Ipswich have their first effort of the game but Fatawu curls over from the edge of the box.

Another fine goal from Isak and Liverpool lead 2-0 not even 10 minutes into this game. It is Gakpo who assists again with a superb pass with the outside of his right foot from halfway into the left channel to pick out the run in behind of Isak. The Swede cuts inside Greaves onto his right before then chopping back onto his left. He then coolly slots home past Scherpen and Liverpool have the dream start.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

Liverpool take a deserved lead at Portman Road. Kerkez wins the ball back for Liverpool on halfway and the ball comes to Gakpo. The Dutchman drives forward and spots Isak in space to his right. Isak’s movement is very clever as he drifts off the defender into space. He takes a touch before smashing the ball past Scherpen at his near post. Should Scherpen have saved that? Possibly but Isak did hit that very hard. For the first time this season, Liverpool lead in a Premier League match.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

Wirtz is penalised for a very soft foul on Enciso, who just threw his hands in the air after the slightest bits of contact. The referee Darren England was not initially going to give it but eventually does, giving Ipswich the chance to swing it in from the left into the Liverpool penalty area.

Fatawu swings it in with his left but Alisson punches away.

It has been all Liverpool in these early stages but have yet to have a shot. Ipswich have barely touched the ball thus far.

Liverpool win the first corner of the game as Davis is forced to put it behind after good work from Munoz down Liverpool’s right.

Szoboszlai’s outswinger is headed away from danger.

Andoni Iraola wondered what might happen when he first sat down to talk with Bradley Barcola.

Here was one of the world’s best wingers, with his 13 major honours, 28 international caps and £123m price tag – a combination that could easily lead a man to view himself through the prism of a superstar: never mind what I can do for you, what can you do for me?

Liverpool’s due diligence on Barcola had all been positive – not least from the currently injured Hugo Ekitike, who had been a vocal advocate of his compatriot’s capabilities to the recruitment team – but Iraola wanted to gauge for himself exactly what the 24-year-old was going to offer.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

Team news from Portman Road to follow shortly.

#1864. Leeds United 1 Tottenham 0: Personality counts as Daniel Farke has everything that Roberto de Zerbi doesn't possess

Organisation, obduracy. Watching each other’s backs and sticking together.

Strong minds, intensity and feeding off the five-star fuel which is in abundant supply when Leeds attack the Gelderd End, particularly in the second half of matches.

Did you know with a Digital subscription to Yorkshire Post, you can get access to all of our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

More especially when those present sense that one of the so called ‘name’ clubs don’t particularly fancy it on a November day in Yorkshire.

It was a win for the home dressing room and the culture that Farke has carefully constructed. He knew it - unity and commitment were the first two words he used to describe his side’s first victory in six games - and his Spurs counterpart Roberto De Zerbi also knew it too.

These are the sort of wins that proper managers love. Ones that are hewn from a bit of adversity. Conversely, they constitute defeats that tell a lot to the vanquished.

De Zerbi said that his side lacked ‘personality’ in the second half and he was spot-on. Personality counts in tight matches.

And while Noah Okafor may have only been on the pitch for just over a minute and a half before his match-winning strike 11 minutes from the end of normal time, nobody could say that the hosts’ breakthrough wasn’t coming or deserved.

Yes, Spurs were entitled to feel hard done by what happened - or didn’t - in the 37th minute with Mathys Tel. Ultimately that wasn’t the point.

A lengthy VAR check scrutinised Jayden Bogle’s challenge on the Spurs man close to the near touchline. The Leeds defender’s left-boot raked the back of Tel’s Achilles, leaving the Frenchman writhing in agony for a short while. Briefly, he did manage to continue before succumbing. Tel left Elland Road in a protective boot and on crutches.

In a post on X, the Premier League Match Centre later confirmed Bogle’s action was viewed as accidental and at low speed. It spared him from a red card, despite seemingly setting a precedent, as similar recent challenges from Jean-Phillipe Mateta and Ryan Sessegnon were deemed sending-off offences.

Spurs submitted a subsequent complaint to Pro Ref following the latest incident. But it was not the reason why they lost. Saturday served as a reminder that when things don’t go in the direction that you like, you show character and crack on.

In the second half, a group of players - several brought in at considerable expense in the summer - lacked cojones, as the Spanish say.

De Zerbi might be Italian, but he wouldn’t need to be told what it meant. He is still finding out about his group as a collective. Farke knows everything about his own and implicitly trusts them.

His Leeds side weren’t bad in the first half, but they weren’t particularly good either. Spurs possessed more of the poise on show. Mateus Fernandes - rightly cleared of a handball offence by an early VAR check - was prominent.

Seeking a fourth successive Premier League win for the first time in over 1,000 days, the visitors laid a decent platform without forging a lead in the opening half.

The second half was a different story. Leeds’ senior professionals in the likes of Dominic Calvert-Lewin and Ethan Ampadu took over.

Their eyes lit up and sensed Spurs uncertainty, while the unforgiving Leeds crowd reminded the visitors of their location south of the Watford Gap. Soft was the polite word employed.

Unlike those in white, the ones in indigo couldn't get going. Leeds, for whom Melvin Bard made an excellent impression after coming on for Gabriel Gudmundsson (hamstring) starred to become incessant in a half when they posted 13 goal attempts.

Nico Elvedi headed a rebound wide after Calvert-Lewin caused consternation. Ao Tanaka spurned a terrific chance, while Antonin Kinsky later made a splendid reaction save to tip over a hooked effort from the recalled Sean Longstaff.

De Zerbi had made a treble change to try and change the narrative. Farke played the telling cards.

Bard's throw-in on the left was flicked on by Calvert-Lewin. Replacement Harry Wilson challenged Rodrigo Bentancur and the ball dropped invitingly for Okafor, who did the rest. On the pitch for just 97 seconds, it was the quickest goal by a top-flight substitute this season.

The number for Spurs to mull over was 51 - the amount of Premier League games in which they have failed to win after going behind.

The late onslaught never came, although James Trafford made one key late save to deny Jan Paul van Hecke. After Bournemouth, that was important.

Leeds United: Trafford; Justin, Elvedi, Muharemovic; Bogle (Rodon 93), Ampadu, Longstaff (Greuv 93), Tanaka (Wilson 77), Gudmundsson (Bard HT); Nmecha (Okafor 77), Calvert-Lewin. Substitutes unused: Zetterer, James, Aaronson, Bijol.

Tottenham Hotspur: Kinsky; Porro (Gallagher 65), Van Hecke, Van der Ven, Robertson; Tonali, Fernandes (Bentacur 65), Gray; Kudus (Williams-Barnett 83), Tel (Solanke 43); Marmoush (Kulusevski 65). Substitutes unused: Gunter, Senesi, Maddison, Davies.
